description: Revocation closure `retraction-after-correction` over the 57-entry toy corpus (core spec §5.1, §5.3), evaluated at the checkpoint committing the trigger.
note: Record A was corrected twice earlier in the corpus — to A2 at entry 6 and to A3 (hmac-sha256:0879bc168b342470d4a069d1f6df5b42214dc494b43d1d7494821dc23438faf6) at entry 12 — and is now RETRACTED outright at entry 18. Core spec §5.1: "For a retraction on (ds, X), the seed set is exactly {(ds, X)} — retractions never seed superseded replacements." So the seeds are {A} alone, and the consumers of A2 — S1' (sha256:e4fccbcb05345bc70f1327bb001a1bb09f85df01de4e35b3778089aed70f24c4) at entry 7 and W1/W2 at entry 10 — are NOT affected. Retracting A says nothing about A2: A2 is a separately introduced record with its own history. Contrast `supersession-chain`, where a *correction* of the same original does seed A2, because that correction supersedes the one that produced it.
